partes.p: Suppose that $f(0)$, the price of wine when first bottled, is a Cobb-Douglas function of the weather:
$$f(0) = \delta_{t}W_{t}^{\beta}H_{t}^{\gamma}, \text{ for a wine bottled in year } t, \tag{2}$$
$W_{t}$ is the average rainfall in August and September
$H_{t}$ is the average temperature in July and August
$\delta_{t}$ is an unobserved random shock that is independent of $W_{t}$ and $H_{t}$
Estimate and $\beta$ and $r$ assuming $\gamma = 0$. What impact does the inclusion of data on rainfall have on your estimate of $r$? Why?
Estimate $r$, $\beta$, and $\gamma$ together. How does your estimate of $r$ change? Why?
Construct an F-test of the joint hypothesis: $\beta = 0$ and $\gamma = 0$.
